name: Dark Beige
lede: Dark Beige is a muted, yellowish modifier on [[beige]], recorded in the 2010 xkcd color survey and, under near-identical names like Dusky Yellow and Old Ivory, one of the most common colors in our painting archive.

sections.title: A modifier with many aliases
sections.body:
The name follows the library's modifier grammar, *dark* plus [[beige]], and its only catalogue record is the 2010 xkcd color survey, an open web poll [1]. Our library groups a cluster of older, separately-sourced names as close enough on screen to call the same color: California Green, Dusky Yellow, Fog Yellow, Old Ivory and Powdered Gold among them, none of which share the xkcd survey's history [1]. Which, if any, came first is not something our sources settle [2].

Its nearest named neighbors by color distance are [[dust]] and [[ecru-olive]], both almost indistinguishable at 2.6 to 3.0 units [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color this close to Dark Beige is one of the most common in our archive: 4,263 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, almost 18 percent, more common than 97 percent of the named colors we track [4]. It peaks in paintings from the 1400s and is most overrepresented in paintings from Iran, at 3.1 times expected [4]. Cornelius Norbertus Gijsbrechts is its most devoted painter, carrying it in nine of nineteen works here, 3.3 times the baseline for his museums [4]. In printed English the phrase itself peaks in the 2010s, centuries after the hue was common in paint, since Ngram counts the words, not the color [4].
